summary: Accept-queue flood causing prefetch lock contention and elevated 5xx (502/504) error floor
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13T18:20 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (primarily 502/504) for requests from customer Acme ChatOps on the us-east serving pool. Impact: customer-facing API calls were failing at ~6-12% error rate for ~2 hours, causing degraded user experience and retries. Symptoms point to an accept-queue flood at the API gateway combined with heavy prefetch activity that caused kvcache shard locks and upstream runtime worker stalls leading to watchdog restarts and 502/504 from gateway.
impact: Large volume of requests from one dedicated tenant caused sustained 5xx floor (~6-12%). Reported by customer as >30% session failures during peak period. Billing unaffected but SLA degraded; customer on dedicated plan requested immediate mitigation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a tenant burst with 300 concurrent long-text generation requests (avg prompt length 2k tokens) against redwood/opt-6.7b pinned to a dedicated pool.
2) Each request triggers prefetch for KV shards due to cold KV entries.
3) Observe accept queue growth on API gateway and threadpool backlog on serving runtime; kvcache shard mutex contention increases and prefetch workers block.
4) Watchdog kills blocked runtime workers leading to upstream 502/504 responses from API gateway.
timeline_of_events: 2026-03-13T18:12 UTC - Customer reports increased errors via support channel (#support-customer-acme)
2026-03-13T18:20 UTC - Monitoring alerts: apigw 502 rate rises from 0.3% -> 6% (rolling 5m)
2026-03-13T18:28 UTC - SRE observes accept queue growth and concurrent connections spike + prefetch QPS growth 12x baseline
2026-03-13T18:35 UTC - First mitigation: apply emergency tenant-level soft-rate-limit (20rps) and enable fallback model routing
2026-03-13T19:05 UTC - Error rate drops to ~1.2% after partial draining and scaling actions
2026-03-13T20:10 UTC - Deploy patch to prefetch code with per-shard try-lock and backoff (hotfix PR merged) - see PR 1842
2026-03-13T20:35 UTC - Autoscaler adds +2 worker fragments to dedicated pool; KPI stable
2026-03-14T10:00 UTC - Post-incident review started; investigation continues into long-term fix and alert tuning
investigation_notes: Accept queue telemetry: connection backlog peaked at 8k queued requests on a single ingress instance; connection churn high (short-lived connections)
KVCACHE behavior: prefetch threads acquired global mutex when encountering cold keys. Under burst this produced head-of-line blocking across many concurrent sessions.

Runtime observations: blocked prefetch worker threads held pinned CPU and scheduler slices; some runtime processes hit watchdog timeout and were restarted by the runtime supervisor; restarted processes caused in-flight fanout to return 502s.
Heap / GPU: no GPU OOMs observed; metrics show CPU load high on proxy/worker threads rather than device memory pressure.
Hypothesis: combination of accept-queue flood + per-request aggressive prefetch caused synchronous global lock contention that cascaded into runtime stalls and restarts.
Correlated signals: high prefetch error/timeout count, increased mutex wait times in kvcache, elevated process restart counter on a subset of serving nodes.
Customer traffic pattern: Acme ChatOps had a scheduled load test at 18:15 (unannounced) that sent many long prompts concurrently; customer engineering team confirmed approximate test at 18:10-18:25.
mitigation_actions_taken: 1) Immediate soft-rate limit applied to tenant (20rps).
2) Enabled fallback routing to smaller model variant (gpt-small-v2) for non-critical endpoints to reduce prefetch pressure.
3) Increased serving pool by +2 worker fragments and added capacity fallback in us-east.
4) Hotfix deployed to prefetch to use try-lock + exponential backoff (PR 1842) to prevent global blocking.
5) Temporarily increased watchdog timeouts to reduce noisy restarts while we validated lock fix.
6) Customer asked to pause scheduled load tests until safe window.
resolution_notes: Root cause: synchronous prefetch implementation used a coarse-grained lock per kvcache that under tenant burst turned into a global bottleneck. That bottleneck produced runtime thread stalls and watchdog restarts which surfaced as upstream 502/504 waves at the gateway. Fix: hotfix reduces lock contention by switching to per-shard try-lock with bounded backoff and added metrics to surface mutex wait percentiles. Post-fix validations show steady 5xx floor <0.5% under similar synthetic load. Permanent follow-ups scheduled to refactor prefetch to async IO model.
postmortem_actions_and_followups: 1) Engineering: schedule design work to move prefetch to async non-blocking model (owner: @evan-kim, due 2026-04-10)
2) Observability: add kvcache lock wait time SLI and set alert at 1% sustained (owner: @sre-oncall, due 2026-03-20)
3) Release: include hotfix in next minor runtime release and run canary traffic tests (owner: @miguel-torres, due 2026-03-18)
4) Support: update tenant onboarding docs to recommend staged load tests and pre-notification for dedicated pools (owner: @support-lead, due 2026-03-22)
5) Customer: run joint verification with Acme ChatOps for their traffic profile in non-prod  (owner: @solutions-eng, due 2026-03-19)
